text: When setting project goals, the SMART framework is incredibly useful. This means your goals should be Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. For example, instead of "improve the website," a SMART goal would be "increase website traffic by 20% within three months." To reach this, you can break the project into milestones and deliverables. A milestone might be completing the website design, while a deliverable could be the final design file. Finally, ensure stakeholder alignment—everyone involved, from team members to managers, must agree on the goals and expectations. This prevents confusion and keeps the project on track.
